item.content:encoded:
This creeps me out. The rapid desensitization is terrible way to die, and the exploration log sells the horror of sudden isolation despite actual physical proximity.

The transmission of the effect in the phone call has some nasty implications too, making it hard to figure out what the "blackbox" actually is. Thaumatological investigation seems dangerous, though I'd like to see an attempt with a drone and cycling operators.

+1

item.content:encoded:
Yeah, shame the rest of the team missed the deadline. I guess I could work on it as a standalone, or maybe something separate.

I did the format without using quote boxes because I got sick of writing in them, and I thought they looked less clean than the divs. In terms of structure, I guess I aimed for something less organised. It felt awkward to write an organised document about something nobody really understands.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I found this GOC format serviceable but not exactly spectacular. Granted, I'm not the most familiar with the format.

From a Doomsday perspective (I understand this is only a first entry to an unfinished storyline), a slowly expanding field that removes all sensitisation is unique enough. I found that this seemed realistic enough as well, and works as a "all parties involved have no damn idea what's happening". I just wish I was able to see more, so I'm curious if you have something more planned outside of the contest?

Like I said, it's nothing groundbreaking but it works for me. +1
